skill.name: context-receipts
skill.description: Emit privacy-safe receipts for context selection, deferral, hydration, compaction, pruning, delegation, usage attribution, and boundary handoffs.
skill.summary: Create privacy-safe receipts for context boundary decisions and audit gaps.
skill.author: caioribeiroclw-pixel

security_audit.summary: I reviewed README.md and SKILL.md against the static findings. README.md paths are fixed documentation links or example commands, while SKILL.md matches are documentation markup and event names. No semantic prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or malware behavior was found.

remediation.issue: README.md uses parent-relative example paths that look like traversal to automated scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the example paths with repository links or state that the commands are optional fixture checks outside the installed skill.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md uses many backticked event names and fenced examples that automated scanners misread as shell execution.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short note that the blocks are illustrative receipt shapes and no commands run from the skill.

content.value_statement: Context-heavy agent workflows can hide what data crossed tool, memory, and subagent boundaries. This skill guides concise receipts that prove routing, privacy, and remaining audit gaps.
actual_capabilities: Guides privacy-safe receipts for Tool Search and lazy MCP loading.
Defines receipt fields for runtime tool-surface changes.
Tracks retrieved-context delivery, acknowledgment, and citation.
Documents subagent MCP exposure and ToolSearch propagation checks.
Captures compaction, pruning, delegation, and usage attribution audit gaps.
Encourages hashed IDs, counts, buckets, and raw-content exclusion flags.
limitations: It is markdown-only guidance; it does not run validation or create receipts by itself.
It proves boundary behavior, not answer correctness or tool relevance.
It relies on the agent or harness to emit truthful receipt data.
Example commands reference repository fixtures that may not exist after standalone installation.

use_cases.title: Audit Tool Search rollouts
use_cases.description: Verify that lazy MCP loading keeps full schemas deferred until a tool is selected.

use_cases.title: Verify retrieved context use
use_cases.description: Check that required context was delivered, acknowledged, and cited before edits or tool calls.

use_cases.title: Review compaction boundaries
use_cases.description: Record what pruning, compaction, or delegation changed without exposing raw transcript content.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic receipt
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for one context-saving workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a privacy-safe context receipt for this workflow: [describe workflow]. Include selected context IDs, suppressed item counts, raw-content flags, and audit gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Check retrieved context
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of GraphRAG, memory, or code search.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this retrieved-context workflow and produce a receipt showing which context was delivered, acknowledged, cited, suppressed, or missing.

prompt_templates.title: Audit subagent tool exposure
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of delegated agents and MCP policy.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a receipt for this subagent run. Show intended tool exposure, declared tools, actual tool surface, deferred definitions, and boundary gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a full boundary audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced multi-stage audit across tools, memory, compaction, and delegation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a complete context-boundary receipt plan for this agent workflow. Cover Tool Search, retrieval, usage attribution, compaction, delegation, and privacy defaults.

output_examples.input: A team uses lazy MCP loading and wants proof that full schemas stayed deferred.
output: Receipt summary lists index-only startup, selected tool ID, suppressed tool count, redacted call status, and an audit gap.
The receipt confirms that raw schemas, arguments, and results were not copied.

output_examples.input: A reviewer wants evidence that retrieved baseline context was used before an edit.
output: Receipt summary shows required context IDs, delivered IDs, acknowledged IDs, cited IDs, and missing-context stop behavior.
The receipt states that raw documents, paths, and transcript snippets stayed out.

output_examples.input: A manager agent delegates a large investigation to a child agent.
output: Receipt summary records the delegated task category, child output size bucket, returned summary size, and parent boundary status.
The receipt identifies any audit gap about the quality of the returned summary.

best_practices: Use stable IDs, hashes, counts, and token buckets instead of raw private content.
Always record what crossed the boundary, what stayed out, and what remains unproven.
Include explicit raw-content flags for prompts, schemas, arguments, results, transcripts, and paths.
anti_patterns: Do not copy raw prompts, raw tool schemas, raw tool results, secrets, or full transcripts into receipts.
Do not claim that a receipt proves answer correctness or tool relevance.
Do not summarize boundary behavior with vague statements such as enabled, used, or optimized.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps teams prove what context crossed an agent boundary without exposing private source material.

faq.question: Does it create receipts automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides receipt patterns and checklists for an agent, harness, or reviewer to apply.

faq.question: Can receipts include private prompts or tool results?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly recommends hashes, IDs, counts, buckets, and redaction status instead.

faq.question: Does a receipt prove the agent made the right decision?
faq.answer: No. It proves routing and boundary behavior, while semantic quality remains an audit gap.

faq.question: Which workflows are covered?
faq.answer: It covers Tool Search, lazy MCP loading, dynamic discovery, retrieval, usage attribution, pruning, compaction, and delegation.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Platform engineers, AI application developers, and security reviewers can use it to audit context-handling workflows.
